newsitem.title: ITALY: UN finds hundreds of "living skeletons" in S.Leone.
newsitem.headline: UN finds hundreds of "living skeletons" in S.Leone.

text.p: The U.N. World Food Programme said on Friday it had found hundreds of emaciated people in Sierra Leone who looked like "living skeletons" after being held by rebels as slave labourers for up to five years.

The WFP said thousands of other people may have been been held captive by rebels. "The people we saw looked like a group of living skeletons with bundles of rags on their heads," a statement quoted the WFP's director in Sierra Leone as saying.

Local WFP officials, after hearing reports that hundreds of sick and hungry people had walked long distances in a desperate search for food, said they had found a "horrific scene" at the town of Blama.
"Men and women were reduced to skeletons, with some of them having to support themselves on sticks to walk," the statement quoted the WFP country director Mohamed Diab as saying.

"Young men and women, besides being very thin, had swollen feet and sores, having walked days to reach Blama. The children had bloated stomachs, scabies and discoloured hair because of malnutrition," Diab said.

He said the people had recently been freed by hunters organised into a civil defence force by local leaders after being held "as forced labour" by Revolutionary United Front Rebels for up to five years.
